title: Rollout Scenario Canvas and Quick-Restore Prototype
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact, scenario-driven canvas in the Redwood Console that lets operators compose rollout scenarios (canary, A/B, staged splits) and immediately rehearse failures with a one-click Quick-Restore. The canvas should surface expected latency/cost/SLO impact for each scenario, provide time-travel simulation of traffic shifts, and expose rollback triggers and escalation steps. The goal is to reduce time-to-decision during incidents by making trade-offs and rollback actions discoverable, reversible, and testable before going live.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas supports composing up to 4 variant routes with percentage controls and named segments
Simulation mode animates traffic shift over a chosen window and shows delta projections for latency, cost, and error rate
Quick-Restore action visibly reverts traffic to last known-safe variant and creates a pre-filled incident runbook entry
UI includes an unambiguous confirmation flow and keyboard shortcut for Quick-Restore (Cmd/Ctrl+R) in emergency mode
Design handoff artifacts include component specs, responsive layouts, and interaction prototypes in Figma
flow_summary: 1) Compose: operator adds variants and target segments. 2) Preview: canvas computes projected SLO/cost deltas. 3) Rehearse: run a simulated rollout with step controls and time travel. 4) Promote: schedule or execute the rollout. 5) Emergency: Quick-Restore reverts traffic and surfaces postmortem checklist.
comments: 2026-03-09 Maya Chen: Initial concept sketched — focused on a single-pane workflow that keeps critical SLOs visible next to the percentage sliders. Linked the PRD in Confluence.

2026-03-11 Arjun Patel: Built low-fi flows in Figma; ran usability test with two platform engineers. Key feedback: show absolute traffic numbers in addition to percentages; make Quick-Restore clearly separate from scheduled rollouts.
2026-03-12 Priya Nair (PM): Approved direction for simulation metrics. Requested a toggle to include cost impact per 1M tokens in preview.
2026-03-13 Sam Ortiz (Eng): Noted backend needs to expose per-variant delta metrics and a safe-restore API endpoint. Filed ENG-9875 as dependency.

2026-03-14 Design Review: Internal critique — tighten microcopy for emergency flow, add confirmation cooldown, and design confirmation modal to include 'create incident' checkbox. Assigned Arjun to update prototype.
2026-03-15 Arjun Patel: Updated hi-fi prototype (Figma) with time-scrub simulation and Quick-Restore modal. Pushed component spec draft to repo. Marking patterns for accessibility review next week.
notes: Design should account for Dedicated and Private customers where rollout may span regions. Consider a simplified 'read-only emergency' mode for low-privilege operators. Include copy for auditor logs: every Quick-Restore must create an immutable audit entry with actor, timestamp, and rollout snapshot.
